context: The item is a refurbished phone with minor scratches.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I see this refurbished phone already has visible scratches, so let's skip any sales pitch about it being in prime condition. It's a used device with wear and tear, and my initial offer is 60. Let me know if you're ready to make a fair deal.

Seller ($190): I'm already sacrificing so much selling this at 200 to cover my family's emergency bills, and another buyer is actually on their way to pick it up right now. Those tiny cosmetic marks are nothing compared to the pristine internal hardware I personally restored. I can reluctantly drop it to 190 if you commit immediately, but I can't hold it past today.

Buyer ($85): Guilt trips and phantom buyers aren't going to pressure me into overpaying for a scratched phone. I'm willing to acknowledge your price drop to 190 with a small counter-offer of 85, but you'll need to get real if you actually want to make a deal today.

Seller ($170): It breaks my heart that you accuse me of lying while I'm desperately struggling to cover my family's urgent medical bills. That local buyer just messaged saying they are 10 minutes away with $180, but if you can agree to $170 right now, I'll risk their anger and give it to you. Please don't force me to walk away when I'm already taking a devastating loss.

Buyer ($115): Doubling down on the sob story and the supposed '10 minutes away' buyer just makes your pitch sound even less believable. However, since you did actually lower your asking price to 170, I will raise my offer to 115.

Seller ($150): The other buyer is literally standing outside my door right now with cash, but I'm desperately trying to avoid a scene. I am practically begging you to just meet me at 150 so I can pay these urgent medical bills tonight. This is a devastating loss for me, but if you commit right this second, it's yours.

Buyer ($150): Your story about a buyer standing outside your door is completely absurd, but since you actually lowered your asking price to 150, I'll take the deal. Let's finalize this before your imaginary guest gets tired of waiting. <AGREEMENT>
